 Kerrowan Marine Systems plc  |  Annual Report 2025
2
Chair's letter
Dear shareholder, 2025 was the year in which Kerrowan stopped being a promising mid-sized instrument
maker and started to look like the leader in its niche.  Our people delivered record revenue, a meaningfully
higher margin and a full product launch, all while the business absorbed a change of Chief Financial Officer and
the opening of a new site in the Netherlands.
 I want to begin by thanking Graham Leckie, who retired as Chief Financial Officer in January 2025 after eleven
years with the company.  Graham steered Kerrowan through its move to the main market and through the
difficult supply years of 2021 and 2022.  He was succeeded by Priya Raman, who joined us in February 2025
from a listed engineering group and has already sharpened the way we allocate capital.
 The Board met eleven times during the year, including two full-day sessions on strategy.  Most of that strategic
work went into Course 2028, the plan described on page 6, which the Board approved in October 2025.

Kerrowan Marine Systems plc  |  Annual Report 2025
6
Strategy: Course 2028
Course 2028 is the Group's strategy for the four years from 2025 to 2028.  It was developed by the executive
team over the summer of 2025 and approved by the Board in October 2025.  It replaces the earlier plan, Horizon
2025, whose revenue target of £175m was exceeded a year early.
 The strategy has a simple premise: customers increasingly want answers rather than instruments.  A harbour
master wants to know whether a channel is safe for a deep-draught vessel, not to read raw sonar files.
 Kerrowan is therefore building complete monitoring systems in which its hardware feeds Harbourline, and
Harbourline turns the data into decisions.
 The four pillars
Pillar one, Connected hardware, means that every new Kerrowan instrument will connect natively to
Harbourline from 2026.  Pillar two, Software growth, aims to double Harbourline annual recurring revenue
between 2025 and 2028.  Pillar three, Service close to the customer, extends the model of the Rotterdam
service centre to North America and Asia.  Pillar four, Responsible operations, commits the Group to net zero
emissions from its own operations by 2032.

traffic systems into a single live view of a port or offshore site.  Customers pay an annual subscription based on
the number of connected assets.
 Harbourline generated £26.9m of revenue in 2025, of which £22.8m was recurring subscription revenue.  The
number of port customers using Harbourline rose to 212 at the end of 2025, from 168 a year earlier.  Customer
retention measured by revenue was 108%, meaning that existing customers increased their spending on the
platform by more than was lost through cancellations.
 The most popular new module in 2025 was Channel Depth Assurance, which compares the latest Kestrel
survey with the depth a vessel needs and warns the harbour master when the safety margin becomes too
small.  Eighty-three ports had subscribed to it by the end of the year.
 Harbourline is hosted in two European data centres.

Scotland and the Netherlands.  The Group outsources the production of circuit boards and battery packs but
carries out final assembly, calibration and testing itself.
 Port Lennox, Scotland
The Port Lennox factory opened in 1998 and covers 21,000 square metres next to the Group's headquarters.  It
builds the entire Tidewatch range and houses the main calibration tank, a 40-metre basin in which every buoy is
tested in simulated waves before it is shipped.  In 2025 the factory added a second assembly line for the
Tidewatch T5, which raised its annual buoy capacity from 3,000 to 4,200 units.
 Port Lenham, England
The Port Lenham factory in Cornwall was acquired in 2019 and covers 9,500 square metres.  It assembles the
Kestrel sonar range and builds towfish bodies in its own composites workshop.  Port Lenham worked a double
shift for most of 2025 to meet Kestrel 400X demand, and a further £2.1m was invested in test equipment at the
site.
 Service centres
The original service centre at Port Lennox handles customers in the United Kingdom, Ireland and the Nordic
countries.  The Rotterdam service centre opened in June 2025 in a leased building in the city's port area and
employs 34 engineers.

 Diversity
Women held 38% of leadership roles at the end of 2025, defined as the executive team and their direct reports,
compared with 33% in 2024.  Across the whole workforce, 29% of employees were women.  The median gender

Share ownership
The all-employee share plan was offered for the fourth time in 2025, and 61% of eligible employees now own
Kerrowan shares through the plan.
 The Group introduced a hybrid working policy in 2023 for roles that do not need to be on site.  Most software
and central function employees now work from the office two or three days a week, while factory and field
service roles remain on site.  The policy was reviewed in 2025 and kept unchanged after positive feedback in
the employee survey.
 Recruitment remained competitive, particularly for software engineers and experienced field service
technicians.  The average time to fill an engineering vacancy fell slightly during the year, helped by a new
referral scheme that pays employees a bonus when someone they recommend completes their first six months
with the company.

range, where list prices rose by an average of 4%.

delivery, and over the period of the contract for subscriptions and service agreements.  Large Kestrel systems

summer months and many customers place orders before the end of their own financial year in December.  As a

Cyber security
As more customers depend on Harbourline for live port operations, an attack on the platform could disrupt their
work and damage trust in Kerrowan.  The risk was rated as increased in 2025.  The Group commissioned two
independent penetration tests and runs a security operations centre around the clock through a specialist
partner.
 Supply chain
The risk was rated as decreased, because chip lead times have shortened and a second battery supplier has
been qualified.  The Group continues to depend on Varentis Cells for most battery packs in 2026.
 Product quality
The Kestrel 400X firmware recall showed that a single fault can affect many customers at once now that
instruments are connected and updated remotely.  The risk was therefore rated as increased.  The Group has
added a field-testing stage before software releases and an option to roll back updates remotely.
 Foreign exchange
About 78% of revenue is earned outside the United Kingdom, mostly in euros and US dollars, while most costs
are in sterling.  The Group hedges between 50% and 75% of expected foreign currency flows for the next twelve
months.  A ten per cent strengthening of sterling would reduce annual operating profit by about £3.5m before
hedging.

metadata.window:
Annual bonus measures
The 2025 annual bonus was based on operating profit (50%), revenue (20%), free cash flow (15%) and
personal and safety objectives (15%).  The operating profit target for full payout was £26.5m, which the Group
exceeded.
 Long-term incentives
From 2026, half of each long-term incentive award will depend on the Course 2028 revenue and margin
targets, a quarter on total shareholder return compared with a group of engineering companies, and a quarter
on emissions reduction and Harbourline growth.
 Non-executive fees
The Chair receives an annual fee of £185,000.  Non-executive directors receive a base fee of £58,000, with an
additional £12,000 for chairing a committee or acting as Senior Independent Director.  Fees were last increased
in January 2024.
 The ratio of the Chief Executive's total pay to the median pay of United Kingdom employees was 34 to 1 in
2025.
 The Remuneration Committee also reviews pay and conditions across the wider workforce before setting
executive pay.  In 2025 the average salary increase for employees in the United Kingdom was 4.5%, compared
with 4.0% for the Chief Executive.
 Executive directors are required to build up a holding of Kerrowan shares equal to twice their salary within five
years of appointment, and to keep it for two years after leaving the company.  The Chief Executive already
meets this requirement.
